newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-FRENCH CLUBS LOOK FOR ANSWERS AFTER EURO WOES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FRENCH CLUBS LOOK FOR ANSWERS AFTER EURO WOES.

text.p: French clubs that fared badly in European competition this week will be looking to right some wrongs when they return to league action on Saturday.

Champions Auxerre, given a lesson in European Cup soccer by Ajax Amsterdam in their champions' league match at home on Wednesday, have the chance to iron out problems on the visit to bottom club Nancy.
Striker Lilian Laslandes pointed to problems Auxerre would do well to begin to correct against a weak Nancy side.

"I think we should have played more in their (Ajax's) half, press them up front," said Laslandes, who added that Auxerre were creating less chances than when they won the league and cup double last season.
Auxerre need to rediscover the midfield dynamism provided by French international Corentin Martins, who now plays in Spain.
"We no longer succeed in catching our opponents out of position and destabilising a defence," said Laslandes.
Midfielder Moussa Saib and defender Franck Rabarivony, given the run-around by Ajax's tricky Nigerian wing Tajani Babangida, will miss the match through injury.
French clubs made their worst start of the 1990s to European competition this week with three wins, two draws and three home defeats.

Second-placed Lens, guilty of woeful finishing in a 1-0 home defeat by 10-man Lazio in the UEFA Cup on Tuesday, travel to Guingamp, crushed 3-0 by Internazionale on the same night despite a lively performance with a string of goal chances.
Both sides were victims of Italian realism, the visiting teams doing their usual away business of soaking up pressure with solid defending and hitting less Euro experienced rivals on the break.
Lens have lost their way in front of goal after a fine start to the season saw them go top with four straight wins and a 9-3 goals record.
The subsequent 5-1 loss at Monaco apart, they have done better away. They have always gone behind at home this season, even in the 3-1 and 3-2 wins over Nancy and Montpellier respectively.

But these victories were the fruit of a good scoring streak that has since dried up and which they must rediscover over a string of three away games in a row. After Guingamp, they visit leaders Paris Saint-Germain in the league and Lazio in the return leg of their UEFA Cup first round tie in Rome.
Winger Tony Vairelles missed two sitters in front of goal against Lazio and is anxious to forget them by "plunging rapidly back into competition."

PSG, who strolled to a 4-0 win over Vaduz in Liechtenstein in the first step to their defence of the European Cup Winners' Cup on Thursday, visit ninth-placed Cannes looking to retain a zero-goals-against record.
Fourth-placed Monaco, along with PSG the only away winners in Europe, are at home to Lyon.
Montpellier, at home to Le Havre, will be without French internatiopnal goalkeeper Bruno Martini, injured during their UEFA Cup 1-1 draw at home to Sporting Lisbon on Tuesday.
